title: Word 8 — On Repentance
attribution_note: Word 8 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: For those who have sinned after holy Baptism, one hope alone remains: true repentance. Glory to God for this — glory to God, we are not yet lost! Sinners, take heart: hope still remains, the bounty of God is not yet exhausted, repentance is still preached to sinners, good news is still proclaimed to the poor, the mercy of the Heavenly King is still announced everywhere, the doors of mercy are not yet shut, the grace of God still stands open to all, the Gospel and the Lamb of God, *who takes away the sin of the world* [John 1:29], is still preached, the kingdom of God is still proclaimed. Sinners who repent are still saved, and tax collectors and adulterers, cleansed by repentance, still enter the kingdom of God. The merciful God still calls all who have turned away back to Himself, and waits for them, and promises mercy. The loving Father still receives His prodigal sons, returning from a far country; He still opens to them the doors of His house, clothes them in the best robe, puts a ring on each one's hand and sandals on his feet, and bids His whole holy household rejoice over them: “Rejoice, angels, and all My chosen ones! Sinners are turning to Me — people, My own creation, made in My image and likeness. The lost are being saved, the dead are being brought to life, and the wandering are being found.”

Glory to His goodness, glory to His love for mankind, glory to His mercy, glory to His bounty! Poor sinners — why do we linger in a far country and refuse to go to our Father? Why do we perish of hunger? Why do we feed ourselves on lawlessness, like *the husks that the swine ate* [Luke 15:16]? In our Father's house there is abundance of every kind; there even the hired servants have bread enough and to spare. Our Father waits for us with great longing and desire, and when we return to Him from far away, He will look on us with tenderness, gaze on us with merciful eyes, and we shall be dear to Him. He will run and fall on our neck, and embrace us, and kiss us with the kiss of His holy love; He will not reproach us, nor call our sins and lawless deeds to mind, and all His holy angels and chosen ones will begin to rejoice and be glad over us.

sections.heading: Let us hasten to the Father

pairs.en: Let us then come to ourselves, and rise, and go, and hasten to our Father, and say to Him with humility and sorrow: *“Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you, and am no longer worthy to be called your son; make me as one of your hired servants”* [Luke 15:18-19]. Let us hasten, sinners, let us hasten, while time has not yet run out, while the Father still waits, while the doors of His holy house are not yet shut! Let us repent while the mercy of God is still at work, lest we come to know upon ourselves the justice of God — the eternal judgment. Amen.
